messages:
Anya: Quick intake — bringing up a new variant 'llama-13b-q4f' for onboarding. Need a focused perf baseline + quantization impact analysis (p50/p95) across context lengths 512/1024/1536/2048 and batch sizes 1/4/8. Saw a big p95 spike at 2048 in last quick run, want to triage.
Matt: Can you paste the exact bench command, hardware, and raw numbers? Also which runtime/kernel backend was used?
Anya: Command I used:```bash
./bench --model llama-13b-q4f --ctx 512,1024,1536,2048 --batch 1,4,8 --warmup 20 --samples 300 --backend triton --seq-len 2048
```Running on redwood-test-a100 (A100-SXM, CUDA12, Triton2.2). Quick raw outputs below (p50/p95 ms):
- ctx 512: b1 48/82, b4 125/260, b8 220/440
- ctx 1024: b1 72/130, b4 210/480, b8 390/850
- ctx 1536: b1 110/260, b4 360/920, b8 780/1900
- ctx 2048: b1 190/710, b4 820/2400, b8 OOM/timeouts
Anya: Notable: p95 jumps nonlinearly after 1024 and batch>1 causes big tail. Memory pressure likely causing fallback or thrashing.
benchbot: automated: perf-run 1763318400 finished. logs: https://logs.internal/bench/1763318400 (artifact: perf.csv, nvprof.tar.gz)
Jordan: That pattern smells like KV-cache or attention kernel fallback to a slower path when seq>1024. Also check whether Triton kernel supports flash attention for this model config — some ops fall back to cuBLAS path at high seq lengths.
Sophia: Proposed triage checklist (short):
• Isolate cxlen effect: run batch=1 for ctx=512,1024,1536,2048 (no batching) to see pure sequence scaling.
• Batching profile: for each cxlen, try batch 1,2,4,8 with fixed total tokens to measure batching efficiency.
• Backend compare: run same bench with --backend triton, --backend torch, --backend cuda (if available) to spot kernel fallbacks.
• Quant variants: q4f vs q8hf vs fp16 baseline to capture quality/perf tradeoffs.
• KV warmup: run workloads with repeated prefix reuse vs fresh random contexts (cache hit pattern).
• Memory tracing: collect nvprof/nvtx and dmesg for OOM; capture kernel selection logs (runtime debug).
Sophia: Add small acceptance criteria: p50 <= 120ms @ctx512@b1, p95 <= 300ms @ctx1024@b4 for this class to be 'ready-for-serving' baseline.
Matt: I'll own the batching pressure + kv warmup tests. Plan: run isolation sweep (batch=1) today, then batching matrix tomorrow. Assigning to Matt. ETA: first artifacts by EOD tomorrow. @Anya can you upload perf.csv + nvprof tar to the ticket?
Anya: Uploaded artifacts to ticket #ML-835 and noted environment tags. Also attached sample prompts used (short/long).
Jordan: I'll try backend kernel probe — add runtime flag --kernel-debug to emit which kernels are chosen per layer. Can we schedule a 30m pairing if we see fallback?
Anya: Yes please. If kernel fallback confirmed, action options: 1) tune sequence tiling, 2) fallback to alternative kernel (triton->torch) for specific layers, 3) recommend quant profile change (q8hf) if q4f causes memory fragmentation.
benchbot: automated: job Matt/kv-warmup started 1763318460
Matt: Quick note from first batch=1 sweep: p95 scales ~linear until 1024 then grows superlinear after 1536. Will attach csv. Early hypothesis: attention scratch memory allocation spikes causing GPU thrashing.
Sophia: Action items summary: 
• Matt: batching + kv-warmup matrix (artifacts + perf.csv) — ETA EOD tomorrow.
• Jordan: kernel debug probe (flag + nvtx traces) — ETA +1 day.
• Anya: collate prompts, link tickets, verify quant variants to test (q4f,q8hf,fp16) — ETA today.
• Sophia: prepare perf dashboard template (p50/p95/throughput per cxlen/batch) and acceptance criteria — ETA 2 days.
Anya: Thanks team :thumbsup: Let's regroup after Matt posts artifacts. If we confirm kernel fallback, we'll do quick experiment swapping backend and report delta.
Matt: SG. Will ping here when artifacts are uploaded.
Jordan: If anyone hits persistent OOMs, reduce per-batch sequences or try staged KV eviction (small experiment).
Anya: Closing loop for now — marking intake as 'in-progress' on the model-onboarding board.
